title: Traffic failure-mode playbook and KPI SLAs
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, action-first playbook for handling traffic failure modes during activation windows and early-rollout phases. Focus: detect, contain, and preserve user experience while protecting latency and cost KPIs. This doc is intentionally terse — use as a checklist in runbook calls.

Scope:
- Applies to Hosted API + Dedicated routing during phased rollouts
- Covers sudden traffic spikes, tail latency events, model fallback thrashing, cache stampedes, and cross-region failures
- Not a replacement for SRE runbooks; intended for product-ops + oncall alignment and rapid, consistent decisions

Key KPI SLAs (owner: product-ops):
- P50 latency target: <= 120ms (alert: breach >130ms for 10m)
- P95 latency target: <= 450ms (alert: breach >600ms for 5m)
- Error rate target: <= 0.5% (critical: >2% sustained 5m)
- Token cost delta: +/−10% (escalate if +25% vs baseline for 15m)
- Successful fallback score: >= 95% (measure: user-facing success on variant fallback)

Failure-mode matrix (triage shorthand):
1) Spike (traffic > expected baseline * 3):
  - Immediate: throttle non-essential background routes, flip to rate-limited canary, route new traffic to older stable model variant
  - Metrics to watch: ingress qps, queue depth, request timeouts
  - Owner: infra oncall + product-ops coordinator
  - Action window: 0-15 minutes -> containment; 15-60 minutes -> scale decisions or rollback

2) Tail latency spike (P95 jumps, P50 ok):
  - Immediate: set transient sampling to capture full traces, increase KV-cache lookups limits, enable reduced-batch mode for latency-sensitive routes
  - Hotfix: lower max batch size on affected model pool, disable low-priority batching jobs
  - Rollback trigger: P95 > 1s for 10m or user error rate increases

3) Model fallback thrash (rapid variant switches):
  - Symptoms: surge of model-variant switches, repeated user complains, quality regression signals
  - Action: disable auto-fallback loop, pin traffic to last known-good model, roll out canary with smaller traffic slice and manual observation

4) Cache stampede / prefix cache miss storm:
  - Immediate: enable read-through caching, TTL relaxation, and short-circuit identical prefix requests to a single backend call
  - Longer-term: add prefix-reservation heuristics, pre-warm KV for release-critical prefixes

Decision heuristics and thresholds (product-ops quick rules):
- If cost >25% and user-facing errors >1% => throttle non-critical features + notify finance and SRE
- If infra scaling adds >2x capacity cost in a sustained 30m window => evaluate rollback to stable traffic slice
- If >3 dependent services show degraded health => initiate full rollback and incident bridge

Communications templates (to cut-and-send):
- Slack: "@oncall product-ops: Traffic spike detected on /v1/generate. P95 at 720ms, error rate 1.8%. Containing: throttling non-essential routes and pinning to stable model variant. Standup on #ops-bridge in 5m."
- Customer status page: "We are experiencing degraded performance for some API requests. Engineers are containing the issue; updates every 15 minutes."

Preflight tests to run before major rollouts (20m checklist):
- Run synthetic ramp to 5x projected QPS with latency probes and verify P95 stays under gate (450ms)
- Run model-variant failover cycle and verify fallback correctness and rollback latency
- Validate cache warm-up script on a staging pool with live-like prefixes
- Cost smoke: simulate billing delta for 1-hour sustained ramp to ensure alerts fire

Post-incident postmortem anchors (product-ops):
- Timeline with decisions and owners
- Metrics delta chart (baseline vs incident) for latency, errors, cost
- Root cause hypothesis and mitigation plan
- Action items with owners and dates (remove temporary throttles within 48h, automate any repetitive mitigation within 10d)

Runbook snippets (one-line actions for oncall):
- Pin to stable model: "infra-cli route set model poolA stable-v2 --slice=100%"
- Throttle experimental route: "edge-cli rate-limit set /v1/embeds --limit=50r/s --reason=traffic-spike"
- Toggle auto-fallback off: "console: service x settings: model_autofallback = false"

Simulations to schedule (owners noted):
- Daily smoke during beta week: product-ops + infra run a 30m 3x ramp, verify SLA pass (owner: Priya Kapoor)
- Chaos exercise: simulate single-region degradation while routing policy does cross-region fallback and measure user-visible error window (owner: Jonah Martinez)

Notes / open questions:
- Should we add a dedicated "cost-throttle" route in the API surface for rapid triage? (pros/cons and UX implications)
- Need an automated experiment to detect model thrash earlier than user quality signals

Appendix: quick KPI capture format (copy into incident PM):
- Baseline window (1h before): p50/p95/error%/cost per 10k tokens
- Incident peak window: same metrics
- Containment timestamp and actions taken
- Recovery timestamp and actions taken

This playbook is intentionally operational and conservative in its defaults. If you modify thresholds for a specific release, add a short rationale and the expected rollback plan below the change.

Last edit notes: 2025-12-02 — added cost-throttle suggestion and explicit fallback pin commands.
